title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization for Emergency-Priority Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Emergency-priority traffic signal control requires reducing emergency-vehicle delay while limiting disruption to ordinary traffic. This work investigates a finite-horizon QUBO formulation and compares Exact QUBO optimization, QAOA, CVaR-QAOA, a quantum machine-learning policy, fixed-time control, and max-pressure control in a three-intersection corridor. The study evaluates three traffic-demand regimes, examines the effect of the emergency-priority weight, and compares quantum solutions with the exact QUBO optimum. The optimization-based controllers achieved reliable emergency progression across all tested demand regimes, while max-pressure produced lower ordinary-traffic delay. Increasing emergency priority reduced emergency travel time but increased congestion, with diminishing improvements at larger weights. CVaR-QAOA reproduced the exact QUBO solution more accurately than standard QAOA, although the resulting differences in closed-loop traffic performance were comparatively small.
summary: This work tackles emergency-priority traffic control by formulating it as a QUBO optimization problem solved using hybrid quantum-classical methods. It compares the performance of QAOA and CVaR-QAOA against classical baselines across various traffic demands. The study highlights that while quantum solvers improve the mathematical solution fidelity, the practical impact on closed-loop traffic performance is limited by the surrogate nature of the objective function.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex optimization problem of coordinating traffic signals to prioritize emergency vehicles while minimizing disruption to regular traffic flow.
main_result: CVaR-QAOA demonstrated superior accuracy in solving the underlying QUBO formulation compared to standard QAOA, although the resulting improvements in real-world traffic performance were minor.
method: The study employs a hybrid quantum-classical approach, formulating the traffic control problem as a finite-horizon QUBO, and comparing solutions derived from Exact QUBO, QAOA, CVaR-QAOA, and QML policies.
model_or_system: The system is a signalized corridor with $N$ intersections, modeled using queue lengths for main and side roads. The optimization is formulated as a QUBO, which is mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian suitable for quantum annealers or gate-based quantum algorithms.
key_observables: Emergency-vehicle delay, ordinary-traffic delay/congestion, Mean QUBO optimality gap, Exact-QUBO solution hit rate, and First-action agreement.
important_parameters: Three traffic-demand regimes (balanced, main-road-dominant, side-street-dominant), and the emergency-priority weight ($\lambda_{em}$).
main_assumptions: The QUBO objective function is treated as a finite-horizon surrogate for the true cumulative traffic objective, and the controller only applies the first optimized action at each step.
figures_summary: Figures compare the mean QUBO optimality gap, exact-QUBO solution hit rate, and first-action agreement across different demand regimes for various quantum and classical controllers.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the traffic control problem, formulates it as a QUBO, details the comparison between classical (Max-pressure) and quantum (QAOA, CVaR-QAOA) solvers, and evaluates performance across multiple demand regimes.
why_interesting: The paper provides a concrete, complex optimization benchmark for quantum algorithms (QAOA/CVaR-QAOA) applied to a real-world control problem, allowing for direct comparison of quantum solver fidelity against classical optima.
